title: Software Engineer
bio:
Derick Schaefer is a technology leader, consultant, speaker, and author with more than 35 years of experience building enterprise software and leading engineering organizations. Introduced to Go in 2016, he has championed its adoption across SaaS companies for its simplicity, performance, and maintainability.

He is the author of CLI – A Practical Guide to Modern Command-Line Interfaces (https://moderncli.dev) and Integrating SaaS Acquisitions: A Technical Leader’s M&A Playbook. He is also an active open-source contributor, with projects including the RESERVE macroeconomics CLI, the PortableText package for Go, and Static Cache Wrangler for WordPress. Derick enjoys sharing practical lessons on Go, developer tooling, software design, and engineering leadership.

title: Co-founder & CTO
bio:
Achille has worked as a software engineer on distributed systems since 2011, at both startups and large companies like Twitch, Facebook, Segment, and Twilio.

He has authored and participate in multiple open-source projects such as kafka-go, parquet-go, wazero, and also contributed the GOOS=wasip1 port of Go.

In 2024, Achille co-founded Firetiger to develop agents that help engineers manage their deployments, catalog issues, and apply remediations when defects make it to production.

title: Go Security Team Lead
bio: Roland leads the Go Security team at Google, working on cryptography, transport security, vulnerability triage, and generally keeping Go secure. Before working on the Go team, he worked on the Let's Encrypt project building the certificate authority software which now issues millions of certificates each day.

title: Founder
bio: Jeff Lindsay is a builder and entrepreneur most known for his work and ideas in open-source developer tooling. From webhooks to Docker, Jeff has spent much of his career building and pioneering generative primitives that let developers do more with less.

title: Software Engineer
bio: Simon is a Software Engineer working on the Go Foundation Team at Meta. He focuses on developer experience, infrastructure, and tooling, with a background in platform engineering using Kubernetes, cloud networking, and Go.

title: Senior Staff Engineer, TLM
bio:
Sung leads the Go Platform team at Uber. He works on service frameworks, core libraries, static analysis tools, and Go developer experience tools that powers all of the 2,000+ Go services at Uber.

Prior to Uber, Sung worked on the .NET CLR team at Microsoft.

title: Director
bio: Salah Mahmud began his career writing software before transitioning into medicine and clinical research. Now stepping back from active clinical practice, he combines both disciplines to build high-performance systems for the medical field, including tools to process massive health insurance datasets and screen for drug and vaccine adverse events in low-resource settings. Salah's work is shaped by the need to extract maximum performance from limited computational resources, which led to a deep interest in Go, compiler (DSL) design, and low-level optimization.

title: Senior Software Engineer
bio:
Donia Chaiehloudj is a Senior Software Engineer at Isovalent, where she contributes to the Cilium project, focusing on network policy and cloud-native networking. Her work sits at the intersection of Kubernetes, Linux networking, and eBPF, helping improve how distributed systems are secured and observed at scale. 

She is co-author of Learn Go with Pocket-Sized Projects and has a strong interest in sharing content around Go, networking and eBPF. Donia is also an active member of the developer community, leading a local meetup, organising conferences, serving as a Women Techmakers ambassador and part of the Merge-Forward, a diversity CNCF initiative. Outside of engineering, she enjoys sewing, playing the clarinet, and exploring new hiking trails.

title: Staff AI/ML Engineer
bio: Ravi Sastry Kadali is a Staff AI/ML Engineer building infrastructure for autonomous vehicles, with over two decades of experience across platform integrity, API security, and intrusion detection systems. A longtime open-source contributor in the Go ecosystem, he created go-safeinput, SecurePrompt, and cryptoguard-go, and has landed patches in the Go project itself (golang/go), Kubernetes, etcd, gosec, gqlgen, semgrep, OWASP ZAP, Aqua Security's Trivy, and others. His career spans security and platform engineering at Meta, Microsoft, X Corp, Neustar Security Services, and India's Defense Research and Development Organization (DRDO).

title: Software Engineer
bio:
As the technical lead for the Go programming language, Austin is responsible for the overall technical direction and governance of the Go project. Austin’s tenure at Google spans over a decade, with much of that time dedicated to deep-system contributions, including previously serving as the lead for the Go compiler and runtime. They have a long history with Go, including writing a Go interpreter and debugger as an intern in 2009 and developing Go’s concurrent garbage collector with Rick Hudson in 2015. Their recent focus includes optimizing Go for the latest hardware through projects like the Green Tea garbage collector and native SIMD support, establishing governance structures that serve both Go and the community better, and ensuring Go thrives in a world driven by both human and agentic programming. 

An MIT alumnus with a passion for how programming languages shape thought, Austin balances their work on Go with personal interests in smart home technology, mid-century modern architecture, and the decade-long pursuit of the perfect matcha latte.

title: Software Engineer
bio: Ian is a software engineer based in NYC, working on the Go Security team at Google.  In his spare time, he is a volunteer firefighter.

title: Software Engineer
bio: Vladimir Vivien is a software engineer and a technologist who is passionate about working on open source projects using Go.  He is currently building cloud native solutions for the Kubernetes ecosystem and related open source projects. Vladimir has presented at many tech conferences and is also the author of several books including a book on Go titled "Learning Go Programming".

title: Software Engineer
bio: Robert is one of the designers of the Go programming language. Before Go, Robert worked on Google's V8 JavaScript engine and the domain-specific language Sawzall. He was a founding member of the team that created the Java HotSpot virtual machine and the Strongtalk system. Currently, Robert is mostly focusing on generics for Go. He likes things that "just work."

title: Software Engineer
bio:
Dmitri is a software engineer and an avid gopher. He strives to make software more delightful.

Coming from a game development and graphics/UI background where C++ was used predominantly, he discovered and made a full switch to Go 11 years ago, which lead to increased developer happiness.

In his spare time, he's mostly working on software development tools and exploring experimental ideas. He enjoys contributing to open source, fixing issues in existing tools and the Go project itself.

title: Field CTO
bio: At Antithesis, Akshay helps companies build strong verification gates into software factories. Prior to Antithesis, he’s worked on infrastructure and developer experience at a variety of companies - including leading Uber’s Go team.

title: Backend Engineer
bio: Alexander is a backend engineer at Evil Martians, where he helps startups build modern, scalable, and lasting web applications. Alexander has a passion for crafting clean and maintainable architectures.

title: Senior Software Engineer
bio: Ruslan Kadyrov is a software engineer focused on backend systems and infrastructure, building large-scale distributed systems with Golang, Kubernetes, and gRPC at Mercari.Inc., Tokyo, Japan. He spends most of his time dealing with the less glamorous parts of “clean” abstractions: production outages, security boundaries, and interfaces that looked great in code review but failed under real load. He enjoys turning painful production incidents into concrete engineering lessons and sharing what actually worked and what didn’t.

title: Student
bio:
Takuto is a graduate student in computer science at Chiba Institute of Technology in Japan, pursuing a career as a cloud platform developer. His expertise includes Go, Kubernetes, and cloud-native infrastructure.

He organizes Gophers EX, a project that supports the global expansion of the Japanese Go community. With his experience as a speaker at an international conference, he shares practical approaches for challenging and participating in conferences overseas.

title: Senior Software Engineer
bio:
Navneet Anand is a Senior Software Engineer at Uber, where he builds large-scale distributed systems and developer tooling. His work spans high-throughput backend infrastructure, production reliability, and AI-powered engineering productivity. He has led the modernization of critical platforms serving tens of thousands of requests per second, designed systems that improve observability and operational safety, and built agentic developer tools.

Prior to Uber, Navneet spent nearly eight years at Microsoft, where he worked on Windows Defender and large-scale security detection systems protecting over 1.5 billion devices worldwide.

title: Software Engineer
bio: Michael Matloob is a software engineer on the Go Team at Google.

title: CEO
bio:
Andrew Williams has over 20 years of commercial software development experience across a variety of programming languages and has been a core developer in large open source projects such as Enlightenment, EFL, Maven and Fyne. He has been a founding member of many startups including Scotland’s largest mobile apps agency. Since 2018 he has been focused on Go development and is working hard to apply the high quality design principles of mobile app development to cross-platform applications.

Andrew is the author of "Building Cross-Platform GUI Applications with Fyne" and "Hands-On GUI Application Development in Go" and is also the founder of the Fyne toolkit demonstrated in this presentation.

title: Developer Relations Lead for Go
bio: Marc is the Developer Relations Lead for Go at Google. Before joining the Go team, Marc worked as a Site Reliability Engineer (SRE), giving him a passion for building distributed systems with a focus on resilience and observability.

title: Member of Technical Staff
bio: Simon is a software developer at Tailscale, where engineers fearlessly spin up custom internal tools since it’s fast, secure, and easy. Before Tailscale, he has helped software teams wire custom automations to their Salesforce instances, operated and secured one of the world’s largest HBase deployments, and started Developer Tools teams at multiple startups.

title: Software Engineer
bio:
Katie has been working with Go since 2018, when she joined the Go team at Google in NYC. Katie was the tech lead for the module mirror and checksum database and worked on the security and cryptography team, where she led the design and implementation for adding native fuzzing to the language. After Google, she led the Go tracing libraries team at Datadog with heavy involvement in OpenTelemetry initiatives. 

Now Katie has moved to Tokyo, Japan, where she is working at Mercari as a software engineer on their Platform team, with a focus on making the best possible experience for Go developers.

title: Senior Staff Software Engineer
bio: Chris is a senior staff software engineer at Isovalent@Cisco, where he has been a core contributor to the Cilium and eBPF project for over six years, focusing on networking and security.

title: Software Engineer
bio:
Neil is an experienced software, security, and platform engineer, with a history spanning numerous industries from mobile gaming and web hosting to film & television and agricultural technology. While his most recent focus has been on the safe implementation of LLMs and LLM-derived tooling into engineering workflows, he has spent time in both large enterprises in the financial services space, as well as small startups in numerous fields.

Neil's professional software experience includes Go, Python, Node, Ruby, Groovy, Java, and Perl; while he's also spent time building and managing cloud-native infrastructure and CI/CD pipelines of varying sizes.

Neil currently lives in Southwest Florida, with his wife, three children, one dog, and three cats.

title: Principal Software Engineer
bio:
Garrett is a Software Engineer at Skool where he works on Go backend services that help people build and find their online community. Previously, he worked on platform teams at IDme, CrowdStrike, and AWS delivering highly-available services at scale. He’s especially interested in developer experience and using tools like CI, linting, and automation to shorten feedback loops and keep code review focused on correctness and maintainability instead of style debates.

Outside of work, Garrett is based in Southern California and is usually looking for an excuse to get outside and away from the screen, whether that’s running, hiking, backpacking, or anything in between.

title: Senior Lead Software Developer
bio: Seth has been a software engineer at Capital One since 2020. He has worked on several major Go-based projects, serves as a Go language lead, and maintains the company's internal Go shared libraries. Seth volunteers as a steward of the Go Community of Practice at Capital One and is passionate about building a feature-rich Go ecosystem.

title: Founder & Principal Security Engineer
bio:
Benji fell in love with computers when he started early—building PCs, teaching himself to code, and chasing distributed systems, AI, and security. In 2017, he discovered Go at a SANS (SysAdmin, Audit, Network, and Security) conference and attended his first GopherCon a year later. The community’s pragmatism shaped Benji’s approach of shipping real code, measuring outcomes, and sharing what works. Today, he is the founder of and one of the masterminds behind the GopherCon Challenge Series and trains 160+ engineers a year.

Outside of work Benji is a photographer, PADI‑certified SCUBA diver and a relentless bread‑baker chasing the perfect sourdough.

title: Principal Software Engineer
bio: Derek is the creator of Delve, the debugger for the Go programming language, and a contributor to the Go compiler and runtime. He has been developing software for over a decade and has traveled the world speaking at conferences and teaching workshops about debugging.

title: Managing Partner
bio:
Bill is a managing partner at Ardan Labs in Miami, Florida. Ardan is a group of passionate engineers and business professionals focused on building and delivering reliable, secure, and scalable solutions. Bill is also the author of Go in Action and the Ultimate Go Notebook, plus the author of over 100 blog posts and articles about Go. Lastly, he is a founding member of GoBridge and the GDN, which are organizations working
to increase Go adoption through diversity.

title: Professional Open Source Maintainer
bio: Patricio (a.k.a. Pato) is a mechanical engineer turned Go enthusiast. He has used Go to model the physics of rockets and printed circuit boards, and has applied it in embedded systems for a rocket engine test stand as well as in controlling biological processes involving cell cultures.

title: Go Author & Trainer
bio:
Cory is a full stack technologist with nearly 30 years of professional experience. He began his career at CDW.com in the late 90's, where he helped build one of the world's first ecommerce engines, predating Amazon. He has started several technology companies, including Pulsity, a web consulting firm in the late 90's. From that company, Local Launch, an internet marketing technology company, was formed and later sold to RH Donnelly in 2006. 

Cory has years of experience in the Go world, having worked on the Core engineering team that contributes to InfluxDB, a highly scalable, distributed time series database written in Go. He has worked on several other Go projects with a focus on profiling and optimizing applications, using advanced profiling concepts such as torch graphs and tracing profiles. He also has deep ties to the Go community, having started one of the very first Go meetups in the world, Denver Gophers, as well as assisting in the very first GopherCon. He has created and led numerous Go workshops and training courses, has published several online articles related to Go, and co-authored "Go Fundamentals". Cory is also a partner at Gopher Guides, the industry leader for Go training and conferences.

When Cory isn't working on writing new Go training material, he volunteers as a high school AI Programming Club leader. He also volunteers his time helping local entrepreneurs start up their own businesses by offering free business advice and services, such as incorporating their business, getting their web presence set up, and giving them the moral support they need to make their dreams a reality.

title: Principal Software Engineer
bio: Johnny is a software engineer specializing in Go, AI engineering, cloud architecture, and distributed systems. He is a Principal Software Engineer at Stable Kernel and co-founder of a cloud-based SaaS platform focused on workforce development. He serves the Go community as a conference Program Chair for GopherCon. His work appears on platforms including O’Reilly, LinkedIn Learning, and Packt.

title: President
bio: Erik St. Martin spent the last decade building distributed systems for large enterprises such as cable providers, credit bureaus, and fraud detection companies, and now works for Microsoft as a Principal Software Engineer. He co-authored a book on the Go programming language, is the president of Gopher Academy, and emcees GopherCon, the annual conference for the Go community.

title: Technologist For Hire
bio:
Ron is an award-winning software developer and expert in robotics/IoT/computer vision who is very active in the free and open-source community. He has helped many clients such as AT&T, Intel, Sphero, and Northvolt solve some of their most difficult technical and business problems.

Ron is a code contributor to many open-source hardware/software projects and is one of the maintainers of TinyGo (https://tinygo.org), as well as the creator of the open-source IoT/robotics framework Gobot (https://gobot.io), computer vision framework GoCV (https://gocv.io), and embedded WebAssembly framework Mechanoid (https://mechanoid.io)

title: Senior Software Engineer
bio:
Samantha Kendziora is a Senior Software Engineer at Diagrid, where she works on the AI team building developer tooling for autonomous agents and mission-critical workflows. She is a maintainer across the core Dapr ecosystem, a graduated project of the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, including runtime, SDKs, and the Dapr Agents framework (Python) working across both the Go-based runtime and ecosystem integrations. She recently helped drive Dapr Agents to its official, stable v1.0.0 release, shaping APIs and advancing the developer experience for agent-based applications. In addition to her open-source work, Samantha contributes to the Diagrid Catalyst platform, helping evolve Go-based microservices that power scalable, production-grade systems for AI workloads.

Prior to this, she built containerized computer vision applications for healthcare/smart cities and Go microservices for industrial edge environments for naval research. She is a published Go technical author, 2023 Society of Women Engineers Rising Technical Contributor Award recipient, organizer of the Women Who Go meetup in Austin, proud member of several of the Working Groups in the Linux Foundation Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), and serves on the Texas State University Industry Advisory board as an advocate for empowering early-career and underrepresented engineers.

She has spoken at major conferences including:

•	2025 GopherCon US: Go with the (Work)Flow: AI-Driven Code Generation for Workflows
•	2024 GHC Level Up Lab (workshop): Spike Your Application Development Skills with Dapr
•	2023 OSS: A Guide to Dapr: Open Source APIs & SDKs for Developers
•	2022 GopherCon US: A Journey Through Integration Testing with Go - What Could Go Wrong?

Outside of work, Samantha enjoys staying active, working on various house projects, and attending technical events with her family of “gophers,” including her twin sister. She is also currently preparing for her honeymoon after GopherCon in Croatia, Montenegro, Bosnia, and Greece!

title: Group Product Manager
bio:
Cameron is the product lead for the Go programming language at Google and a contributor to Google’s agent ecosystem and AI developer assistance strategy. Before Go, he led Google Cloud's programming languages support and integrations. Before joining Google, Cameron led a high-frequency market-making firm where he built low-latency trading systems in C and C++. 

He likes Go more.

title: Senior Software Engineer
bio:
Cassie Coyle is a Senior Software Engineer at Diagrid, where she works on the Dapr open source project, a graduated CNCF project, building the distributed systems foundation that keeps AI agents and workflows running in production. Cassie is a maintainer of the Dapr runtime and various core Dapr repositories and SDKs, helping shape the roadmap and architecture of the platform that powers durable workflows, crash-safe agents, and fault-tolerant microservices.

Cassie has built extensively across Dapr, including the distributed Scheduler - a horizontally scalable system for reliable job execution - and Workflow History Propagation, a first-of-its-kind capability that brings verifiable execution lineage and chain of custody to durable workflows. As a core member of the Dapr release team, she regularly cuts releases and drives cross-cutting initiatives spanning observability, SDKs, control plane services, and developer experience.

Before joining Diagrid, Cassie helped develop HashiCorp's Waypoint, streamlining application building, deployment, and release across platforms. Prior to that, she helped build out Charles Schwab's cloud infrastructure as part of a major initiative to migrate the company's applications,
including Schwab Bank, to the cloud, building and prototyping the infrastructure pipelines and automation that enabled the transition at scale.

In 2025, Cassie received the Society of Women Engineers (SWE) Rising Technical Contributor Award, given to only 20 women globally each year. Cassie serves on the Call for Papers review team for various conferences, is a member of Dapr Day 2023/2024 and AppDeveloperCon North America 2024 program committees, organizes the Women Who Go meetup in Austin, TX, and is a member of several Working Groups in the Linux Foundation Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF). She enjoys mentoring contributors, and advocating for welcoming spaces for diverse contributors in open source.

She has spoken at major conferences including:

● 2024 GopherCon US: Standardizing Errors in Go: A Practical Guide with Dapr
● 2024 KubeCon NA: Scale Job Triggering with a Distributed Scheduler
● 2024 Open Source Summit: Standardizing Errors: A Practical Guide with Dapr
● 2024 Grace Hopper Celebration: Level Up Lab (Workshop): Spike Your Application Development Skills with Dapr
● 2022 Hashitalks Deploy: Use Waypoint to Easily Deploy to All Three Cloud Providers

Away from the keyboard, Cassie is a beekeeper tending a growing apiary of 7 hives, where she applies distributed systems patterns to build AI-assisted beekeeping tooling. She is part of a family of "gophers" and frequently attends technical conferences with her twin sister, Sam.

title: Founder
bio: Filippo is a cryptography engineer and open source maintainer. He’s been a maintainer of the Go cryptography standard library since 2018, first at Google as lead of the Go Security team, and now as the founder of Geomys, an organization of professional Go open source maintainers.

title: Senior Software Engineer
bio:
Florin is a consultant at Ardan Labs with over 12 years of Go experience. He's worked across distributed systems, application architecture, observability, and cloud infrastructure with time spent at fintech, healthcare, and AI companies like Bread Financial, Press Ganey, drand, and Prediction Guard.

He has worked at AI startups and enterprise companies where he built the infrastructure from the ground up and designed the systems backend from scratch, taking an early-stage platform to something production teams could actually rely on.

Before Ardan Labs, he was at JetBrains as a Developer Advocate for Go where he contributed to the Delve debugger and helped make GoLand the IDE that thousands of Go developers use daily.

Florin's seen firsthand how the jump from AI prototype to production system is where most projects fall apart. His workshop is built around the patterns and lessons he's picked up from shipping AI systems at companies where things have to work.

title: Principal Software Engineer
bio: Jake is a programming language lover and Principal Software Engineer at Microsoft. He currently works on TypeScript, mainly focusing on performance, infrastructure, and the ecosystem, along with side adventures in Go (especially compiler and runtime changes in Go and TinyGo!).

title: Principal Engineer
bio: Vladimir is a mathematician who found his happiness in programming Ruby and Go, contributing to open source, and being an Evil Martian.

title: Principal Engineer
bio:
Casey Manus is a Principal Engineer at Bayer Crop Science and a 30-year veteran of the software engineering industry. Having navigated three decades of evolving technology, Casey has seen countless trends come and go, giving him a unique perspective on building resilient systems that stand the test of time. Today, he applies that deep expertise to solving global agricultural challenges using Go.

A returning GopherCon speaker, Casey previously presented "Genetic Algorithms in Go" in 2023 and continues to remain heavily involved in the Go community and conference.  

Before his long career in tech, Casey served in the U.S. Navy aboard a nuclear fast-attack submarine, an experience that instilled a disciplined approach to complex engineering. Based in Miami, Casey spends his downtime embracing the Florida lifestyle, whether hanging out on his boat in the Florida Keys or enjoying the open water.

title: Creator
bio:
Steve Francia (@spf13) is a familiar face around GopherCon, both as a longtime organizer/speaker and as the former Product Lead for the Go programming language at Google. During his six years leading Go, he helped shepherd the community’s explosive growth from 400,000 to over 4.5 million developers.  

If you’ve built or used a Go tool recently, you’re almost certainly running his code. Steve is the creator of Cobra and Viper, the foundational CLI and configuration libraries powering everything from the GitHub CLI to Kubernetes, as well as Hugo, the renowned Go-based static site generator. Across his open-source projects, he has earned over 195,000 GitHub stars, placing him among the platform's top 50 engineers by project adoption.  

Over his 30-year career, spending 15 of those years in executive leadership at defining tech companies, Steve has made a habit of finding technologies at their inflection point and building the communities that make them permanent. Before Google, he built the developer experience from the ground up as employee #24 at MongoDB, served as Chief Operator during Docker’s hypergrowth to help establish core container standards, and more recently, led AI platform strategy as a Managing Director at Two Sigma.  

A recognized Google Developer Expert (GDE) and GitHub Star, Steve is armed with a philosophy degree that proves surprisingly useful for understanding the human side of software. He is always curious, a father of four, a skateboarder at heart, and writes at spf13.com.

title: Principal Software Engineer Manager
bio:
George Adams is a Principal Software Engineering Manager at Microsoft, where he leads the team responsible for the Microsoft build of Go and related platform integrations. His work focuses on security, cross-platform toolchain engineering, and contributing improvements back to the upstream Go project.

George previously founded AdoptOpenJDK, which became Eclipse Adoptium, now delivering over a billion OpenJDK downloads annually. Coming from a Java and open-source background, he has spent over a decade working at the intersection of large-scale enterprise engineering and community-driven development and regularly keynotes international conferences on open-source governance and secure software supply chains.

title: Software Engineer
bio: Mikayla is a library maintainer at Datadog, based in Brooklyn, NY. In this life, she is a software engineer dedicated to performance optimizations, but in another life Mikayla would be a writer, a brain surgeon, or a wildlife rehabilitator.

title: Engineer
bio:
Sunny is a compiler engineer with experience in language design, performance optimization, and standard library implementation. They have worked on high-performance Protobuf C++ and Rust at Google, and are obsessed with getting the most out of hardware OEMs' parts. They also think that performance should be extremely accessible and frequently writes on the topic.

Sunny is currently at Buf where, unsurprisingly, they focus on Protobuf performance, but also high-quality developer tooling (including Buf's Protobuf compiler frontend).

Outside of software, Sunny is an experienced digital illustrator and painter.

title: Staff Engineer
bio: Dylan has been a professional software developer since 1998, working in the banking, health care, finance, computer security, developer tooling, and now AI industries.  He’s been writing Go full time since early 2016. He is a part-time co-host of the Fallthrough podcast and is an active participant in the Gophers Slack organization. This will be his ninth GopherCon and his fifth time on stage.  Outside of work, Dylan enjoys baseball and golf.

title: Founder & Principal Engineer
bio: Oscar Villavicencio is the founder and principal engineer of M31 Labs, a developer-tools lab built on a shared grammar-surface factory: gotreesitter, a pure-Go tree-sitter runtime with a self-hosting LALR(1) compiler. The factory has shipped eight products since February 2026: Cobalt (COBOL modernization through grammar composition), Manta (GPU inference language), ferrous-wheel, arbiter, danmuji, gosx (batteries-included 3D-native web development framework), fyx, and Markdown++.

title: Software Engineer
bio: Naoki is a Go backend/infrastructure engineer based in Tokyo. He works at Tokyo Software Development, IBM. He has spoken at GoLab 2025 and GopherCon EU 2026, and helps run Go community events in Japan.
